newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European bourses rattled again by Wall St.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European bourses rattled again by Wall St.

text.p: European stocks fell further from record levels on Friday afternoon, rattled by a negative opening on Wall Street which added to fears that the rally in world markets might have run its course.

On currency markets, the dollar weakened against the yen after hitting a 47-month high of 120 yen overnight in Asia but many traders saw it as merely a correction before the bullish dollar reached higher.
In a dramatic reversal after closing at fresh peaks on Thursday, major European bourses tumbled over one percent depressed by an overnight retreat on Wall Street.

And they fell further when Wall Street opened on Friday and promptly chalked up additional losses. New York had been dragged down from record levels on Thursday by waves of sell programs, triggered by negative sentiment in the futures markets.

London was unsettled, falling over one percent from its record close. Supermarket stocks also dropped after J Sainsbury warned that its profits would be well below levels analysts had been predicting.

Fears that the Dow Jones average, which has closed at record highs on no less than 10 occasions so far this year, may be on the verge of a more protracted correction, pushed the FTSE 100 index 48.4 points lower to 4,223.1 at one point before it recovered slightly.
"Markets on both sides of the Atlantic have performed strongly so it's to be expected that we now have a bit of profit-taking," said Corey Millier, UK equities strategist at Credit Lyonnais Laing.
Though every stock in the FTSE 100 blue chip index was marked lower at one point, some traders were reluctant to call an end to the New Year rally.
"So far anyone that has called the peak has been trampled on," said one head of equity sales. "There have been no prizes for standing in the market's way and saying it has changed direction."

Thursday's spurt in London was driven by belief that sterling's recent strength had ended because British interest rates were unlikely to rise soon. A fall in the pound boosted prospects for overseas-earning sectors.

In Frankfurt, stocks on the computerised IBIS index, added to the morning losses when Wall Street opened to register a fall of 1.35 percent by midafternoon. Floor trade, which ended before New York opened, was down 1.16 percent.
But some dealers said it was not the large-scale correction many had feared. "This is not a catastrophe," said one, "It's being seen by some as an opportunity to buy."
French shares also fell steeply as investors, with a nervous eye on Wall Street's performance, took profits.
"I do not see any reason for people to panic. We have had quite a run. It all went up very quickly, and it is now time to pause and take profits," a broker said.
On Thursday, French shares closed at a record of 2,461.25 points on the CAC-40 index, which has risen from 2,193.70 on December 17.
On currency markets, the dollar had a volatile day, falling in European trade after an overnight jump above 120 yen in Asia amid a spate of contradictory Japanese comments.
After poking above 120 yen for the first time in nearly four years, the dollar was driven down by talk of Bank of Japan intervention and confusing remarks about the yen by senior Japanese officials.

Although the dollar dropped to 119.07 yen by mid-afternoon analysts said economic fundamentals were all pointing towards dollar strength and that it would need more than rhetoric from Japanese officials to turn it around.

"Something that would really affect dollar/yen would be some really strong data out of Japan or some weak data out of the U.S. That would be a fundamental cause for a turnaround," said IBJ International senior analyst Roger Francis.
The dollar's rise earlier was fuelled by comments from Japan's Economic Planning Agency that the weak yen was not having a big negative impact on the economy.

But when the dollar hit 120 yen, a Finance Ministry official said Tokyo would not welcome an excessively weak yen and Japan's chief government spokesman said he was confident the yen would not drop below the 120-yen level.
CURRENCIES AT 1515 GMT
The dollar was at 119.07 yen and 1.6280 marks from Thursday's late European levels of 119.50 and 1.6380.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1515 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was down 41.3 points at 4,230.2.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was 26.16 lower at 2,435.09.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was down 35.22 at 2,998.24.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $352.50 an ounce, compared to Thursday's close at $349.45.
